column1: # Known gaps: our open bugs, each one with a todo behind it.
# READ THIS BEFORE ADDING A ROW. A row here is not an accepted difference and it is not permission
# for anything. It is a gap of ours -- a call plain Metal answers and we refuse, or a field that
# differs with nothing announced to justify it -- which, by the owner's standing rule that what
# Metal allows we must allow, is a bug of ours, written down so the one case that holds it visible
# does not make every run red and teach everyone to stop reading the report. An accepted difference
# lives in `docs/API.md` section 10 and is justified; a degradation lives in the degrade catalogue
# and is announced. This file is neither. Nothing here is resolved by being listed.
# It is an EXPECTATION, NOT AN ALLOWLIST, and `conformance replay` holds it to that in both
#   - a refusal or a divergence that is not listed here fails the run: a new gap appeared;
#   - a row listed here that the run no longer holds ALSO fails the run, saying the gap looks
#     fixed and the row must go.
# That second direction is the whole point. Closing a gap forces the ledger edit, so a row cannot
# outlive the bug it stands for and this file cannot rot into a silencer. It also means a row is
# checked by execution rather than by discipline, which is the standard the rest of the suite is
# held to. It has already earned its keep twice in this round: a product fix landed and the replay
# named four stale rows before anyone reasoned about the fix.
# The ledger changes the exit status and nothing else. The report still prints each of these as a
# `Refused` or `Divergent` row, with our answer and Metal's, with Metal's own words where its API
# validation refuses the call too, and counted in the suite's own numbers. Nothing is laundered.
# A row is held only against the cases a run selected and the venues it ran on, so replaying one
# case does not read every other row as fixed, and a run on one venue does not read another
# Tab-separated, SIX fields. Blank lines and lines from `#` are ignored.
#   venue       `*` for every venue, or words held (without case, as a substring) against the
#               venue's own description: its device name, driver, API version and Metal level.
#               `*` is the STRONGER claim, not the looser one -- the second direction then holds
#               the row on every venue the run selected the case on -- so widening a row's scope
#               makes it harder to satisfy, which is what stops a venue-scoped row from becoming a
#               way to silence a venue. A pattern that matches nothing holds the row nowhere, so
#               its gap reads as unlisted and the run fails: a typo is loud.
#   expects     `refused`, a call plain Metal answered and we did not; or `divergent`, a field that
#               differs with nothing announced to justify it. Nothing else is ever written down:
#               an unrecorded case and a stale recording must fail loudly, and a venue that
#               honestly lacks a feature is not a gap of ours at all.
#   site        the site, as node names from the root, exactly as the report prints it.
#   answer      what the run answers there, exactly as the report prints it after the site, which
#               `conformance replay` also emits as a ready-to-paste row so nobody has to
#               reconstruct it. For a refusal that is our typed error. For a divergence it is how
#               much moved: how many of the site's leaves differ and the largest difference where
#               the values are numbers. NOT the first mismatch -- a bound read off the first
#               mismatch is not a bound (four rotated-target rows differ by one code at their
#               first mismatch and reach two well past it), and a walk position is a property of
#               the data rather than of the bug, so it would rename the row whenever an earlier
#               leaf moved. The report prints that position on the line below, where it helps a
#               reader and binds nothing. Part of the row's identity, so a gap that changed into
#               another gap at the same site is a new gap and not this one.
#   waiting on  the open bug, in words: what Metal does, what we do instead, and where the fix
#               belongs. Not matched -- it is what a reader needs -- but a row must carry one.
# A row whose case is not in the tree yet cannot be committed: a test holds every live row to a
# case that exists AND to a site that case's committed recording actually holds, so a row for a
# site the case never produces is impossible rather than silently unheld. Leave such a row here as
# a `#` comment for the stream that owns the case; nothing is waiting today.

column5: Err(Error::Bind("the bind state was refused: Unsupported(Unsupported { feature: MeshShading, needs: NotImplemented, location: None, symbol: None })"))
column6: The runtime refuses `drawMeshThreads` where the threads leave a partial object threadgroup, `Unsupported(MeshShading, NotImplemented)` out of the bind state (crates/metal2vulkan/src/bind/graphics.rs, `mesh_draw`'s `threads[i].is_multiple_of(lo[i])` test), while Metal draws it and runs the threads left over. Not a device gap: this M3 Max has mesh shading and draws every other row of the same probe. Measured on it (macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal, our probe gaps/mesh/obj, one shape per process): the draw launches ceil(threads/L) object threadgroups, `threads_per_grid` is the threads asked for, and the last threadgroup on an axis runs with the threads left over as a non-uniform threadgroup exactly as `dispatchThreads:` does for compute - `threads_per_threadgroup` is min(L, threads - group*L) per axis (6 of 64 reports 6), `thread_position_in_threadgroup` and `thread_index_in_threadgroup` run over that reduced size, `simdgroups_per_threadgroup` is ceil of it over 32, and a threadgroup barrier synchronizes the threads left over alone. The cause is that Vulkan has no partial workgroup: the exact form is the one compute already uses, a region per edge dispatched at its own local size, which for a draw means several draws of several pipeline specializations and, on a grid with more than one whole threadgroup on a higher axis, a primitive order that is not Metal's; the alternative is one draw of ceil groups with the object entry reading its reduced size from its `DispatchRegion` record (`MultiRegion` 1 already carries the grid and L, and already reports ceil threadgroups and the asked-for threads), deriving the thread position and index from `lin` over that size and returning before the body past it, which is exact for everything but a threadgroup barrier and so needs a pipeline variant whose compile refuses an object function that synchronizes. Neither is built. On the orchestrator's todo list as runtime work.

Metal counts the quads the discard drops whole in a simdgroup sum that sits ahead of the discard for a measured reason -- the discard's condition reads the sum (`counted_dependent`), or a device store (`counted_store`) or an atomic (`counted_atomic`) lies between them -- so each kept texel's first channel, `before > after`, is 1. On llvmpipe all four texels of the kept quad read 0, uniformly and each by exactly one code: our run's sum saw the same lane count before and after the discard. MoltenVK on this M3 Max answers Metal's 1 exactly, with no notice, so this is one venue's difference and not the module's rule being wrong (verified: a whole-set replay on each venue, 2026-10-23). The cause is NOT established, and the case as written cannot establish it: the four numbers it records per texel are identical under both candidates -- the device's fragment simdgroup holding only the kept quad, so the dropped quads were never in it (the target is 8 by 4, exactly one 32-lane simdgroup if the device packs it that way), and the device's compiler moving the reduction past the discard although `canon/discard_sink.rs` placed it ahead on purpose. Both give before == after and so (0, 0, 0, 0), on every texel alike, which is why the uniformity across the quad separates nothing either. The next step is the case's: record the simdgroup's own size and the raw `before` and `after` beside the four derived numbers, which separates the two at no cost, then fix whichever it is -- a device whose reduction does not see the dropped lanes needs the active set computed in the module rather than taken from the device's implicit one (crates/metal2vulkan/src/lower/simd/group.rs with crates/metal2vulkan-air/src/canon/discard_sink.rs), and a device whose fragment simdgroup is smaller than Metal's is a different answer again. Open: on the orchestrator's todo list, handed to whoever takes the discard-hoist family.

Metal's `tailSizeInBytes` exceeds our sparse model's on extreme aspect ratios: a 2D texture whose shorter axis is a handful of texels while the longer is a thousand or more. Each row's own two numbers are in its answer field. Measured, and sharper than it was: EVERY one of the 13 differences is a whole multiple of the 16384-byte page -- eleven of them one page, two of them (RGBA32Float, levels-4, 1000x3 and 3x1000) two pages -- and the answers are symmetric in the axes, so 1000x3 and 3x1000 give identical numbers for every format. The page count differs per format, and the rule that produces it is still unidentified; what is now established is that our model is short by whole pages rather than by a rounding, which rules out an alignment or ceiling error inside a page. The rows are scoped to every venue because the answer is CPU arithmetic over a descriptor in `crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/texture/heap_tiled.rs`, the same model on every device at one Metal level: verified identical, site for site and number for number, on MoltenVK on this M3 Max and on llvmpipe in the Linux container (2026-10-23), which is why `*` and not a venue. We believe Metal's answer and our model must both be re-derived before a fix: the model was fitted to ordinary shapes and these are outside what it was fitted to. No tolerance is right here -- the number is a byte count Metal states exactly, and a consumer sizing a heap from it would under-allocate. Open: on the orchestrator's todo list for the sparse stream.

column5: Err(Error::Unsupported("unsupported: Unsupported { feature: Format, needs: NotImplemented, location: Some(RenderPipeline at Color(0)), symbol: None }"))
column6: Plain Metal on this M3 Max makes and runs a render pipeline whose ARGB8Unorm colour attachment blends with DestinationAlpha and OneMinusDestinationAlpha in the COLOUR factors, and stores every texel as the RGBA8Unorm leg's bytes rotated (recorded here over 3 runs, 8,192 texels, zero mismatches; Metal's own API validation let it run). The runtime refuses the pipeline Unsupported(Format, NotImplemented) at colour attachment 0, so the refusal is of something plain Metal does. The cause is structural rather than a policy: the runtime holds ARGB8Unorm in an R8G8B8A8_UNORM image of the rotated bytes, so the image's alpha channel carries Metal's BLUE and a colour factor that must read Metal's destination alpha would have to read the image's red. Vulkan has no such blend factor. The alpha-factor direction is already solved -- a second pipeline output of copies of Metal's source alpha (pipeline::rotated_blend) -- but that trick does not reach a DESTINATION channel, which only the framebuffer holds. The exact forms are a pass that keeps the rotated image's channels in Metal's order behind a swizzled view, or reading the destination in the fragment where the device offers programmable blending. Neither is built. Fix belongs in metal2vulkan's pipeline (rotated_blend) and the runtime's ARGB8Unorm image layout. On the orchestrator's todo list as runtime work.

A Metal SHARED event answers NIL for `device`, and the runtime answers the device it was made on. Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal, a one-off Objective-C probe outside the suite): `[[dev newEvent] device]` answers the device (registryID 4294968395), while `[[dev newSharedEvent] device]` and the event reopened from its `newSharedEventHandle` both answer nil. So `MTLEvent`'s `device` is one answer for a plain event and another for a shared one, and `metal2vulkan-runtime`'s `SharedEvent::device` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/event.rs, the `device` getter the shared event shares with `Event`) gives the device in both. The case's site is the portable form of the getter -- whether the device is the one the case's other objects were made on -- so Metal's nil reads as false and ours as true. Not a device gap: the probe and the case ran on the same chip, and the plain event's getter agrees on both sides. The fix belongs in the runtime's event module, as a shared event answering no device, and it is a one-line change behind a decision the owner has not been asked for: a consumer that reads a shared event's device today gets an answer, and giving it nil is a change to the published API's behaviour. Nothing else of the pair differs -- the label, the handle's label, the reopened label, every value and both waits compare exactly -- so this row is the whole of the difference.

The same gap as `case/handle-round-trip/device`, read on the event `newSharedEventWithHandle:` answered: Metal's reopened shared event answers nil for `device` too (the same probe), and the runtime's answers the device. Two rows because the two sites are two objects' answers and a fix that moved only one of them would leave the other unchecked.

Metal's `MTLComputePipelineDescriptor.reset` is PARTIAL. Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1, build 26A434), from `compute-descriptor-reset`'s own committed recording over three runs: the reset restores the label to nil, every `buffers[i].mutability` to `MTLMutabilityDefault`, `supportIndirectCommandBuffers` and `supportAddingBinaryFunctions` to false and `maxCallStackDepth` to 1, and leaves its three thread-shape properties exactly as the program set them -- `threadGroupSizeIsMultipleOfThreadExecutionWidth` true, `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup` 96, `requiredThreadsPerThreadgroup` 8 by 6 by 2. The runtime has no descriptor object, so the coverage map's counterpart for `reset` is `ComputePipelineDescriptor::new` (crates/metal2vulkan/src/pipeline/descriptor.rs), a fresh value that resets all nine, and our side answers 0, 0 and false where Metal answers what was set. Nothing is announced for it, so by the standing rule it is a gap of ours. It is also very likely an Apple defect rather than a contract: in the same round `MTLTileRenderPipelineDescriptor.reset` restores the analogous `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup`, `requiredThreadsPerThreadgroup` and `threadgroupSizeMatchesTileSize` correctly (`tile-descriptor-reset` is exact) and `MTLMeshRenderPipelineDescriptor.reset` restores every field it has (`mesh-descriptor-reset` is exact), so only the compute descriptor keeps anything. The fix is a choice between two forms and neither may be guessed at: a `ComputePipelineDescriptor::reset` that mirrors Metal's three kept fields, or an accepted difference in docs/API.md section 10 saying a reset compute descriptor keeps its thread shape on Metal and not here. Mirroring an Apple bug in a published crate's API is the owner's call, so this is on the orchestrator's todo list rather than fixed here. Not a device gap: no venue is involved -- the difference is Metal's recorded answer against a plain Rust struct, so the row is every venue's.

Metal compiles a kernel that takes a `visible_function_table` argument and links no visible function, and reflects it: the binding is listed as `MTLBindingTypeVisibleFunctionTable` at buffer 1 (measured on this M3 Max, macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal and under its API validation, which let the case run). The runtime refuses the creation instead: devirtualization (crates/metal2vulkan-air/src/canon/devirt.rs, the `NeedsInput(MissingInput::VisibleFunctionTable)` at the surviving table call) requires the stage to link at least one function of the call's type, on the reasoning that otherwise no entry can hold a callee. Metal's own answer is that such a table is simply null or empty at run time and the shader's `is_null_visible_function_table` and `size()` guards take that path -- which is exactly what `visible_table_caller.metal` does. The fix belongs in devirtualization: where nothing is linked, lower the call site to the null-table behaviour the runtime already documents for an unbound index (a zero-filled neutral, size 0) rather than refusing the compile, so a kernel that only ever reads an empty table still makes a pipeline state. The passing shape of this same case is a second one with linked functions, which needs an `MTLLinkedFunctions` spec in the suite's vocabulary and does not exist yet.

The same gap as the `function-bindings-visible-function-table` row above, reached through an argument buffer instead of a buffer slot, which is why it is a second row and not that one: the refusal names a different input (`buffer: None`, the table having no slot of its own) and a gap's identity here is its case, its site and its answer. Metal compiles `reflection/tables_in_arguments`' `reflection_tables_in_arguments` -- whose argument buffer holds one `visible_function_table<uint(uint)>` at id 0, an inline `uint` at id 1 and an `array<visible_function_table<uint(uint)>, 2>` at id 2 -- with no `MTLLinkedFunctions` at all, and reflects the whole tree: the member and the array elements are `MTLDataTypeVisibleFunctionTable`, and the array carries the stride and argumentIndexStride Metal derived (measured on this M3 Max, macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal; its API validation let the case run). The runtime refuses the creation in devirtualization (crates/metal2vulkan-air/src/canon/devirt.rs:1848, the `NeedsInput(MissingInput::VisibleFunctionTable)` raised where a surviving table call has no function of its type to switch over), although the library itself defines a matching `[[visible]] uint reflection_table_step(uint)`: the function is exported rather than address-taken, so nothing reaches the call site's word and the arm list comes out empty. The fix is the one the earlier row names -- where nothing is linked, lower the call to the null-table behaviour the runtime already documents for an unbound index rather than refusing the compile -- and it closes both rows together, which is the point of keeping them side by side. This row exists because the argument-buffer reach was unmeasured before this case: the earlier row's evidence is a table in a buffer slot, and a claim is only as broad as its evidence. Every other site of this case is unreached while the creation refuses, so the data types its argument buffer states are recorded from Metal and compared against nothing of ours until the fix lands. Not a device gap: the refusal is in translation, before any Vulkan call, so the row is every venue's. Open: on the orchestrator's todo list, with the row above.

`BinaryArchive` has three of Metal's four pipeline adders: `addMeshRenderPipelineFunctionsWithDescriptor:error:` has no counterpart at all. Metal takes the call, takes it a second time with the same descriptor, and then serialises the archive to a file that exists and holds bytes (measured on this M3 Max, macOS 27.0.1, from this case's own committed recording over three runs, plain Metal and under its API validation, which let the case run). Ours cannot be asked: crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/binary_archive/mod.rs declares `add_compute_pipeline_functions` (:138), `add_render_pipeline_functions` (:161) and `add_tile_render_pipeline_functions` (:194) and no mesh form, and the module's own documentation lists the three as if they were all of them. The pieces for the fourth are already there: `metal2vulkan::pipeline::MeshPipelineDescriptor` exists and the runtime creates mesh states from it (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/pipeline/render.rs:629), and the add's own shape is the render one -- create the state with `Some(&used)`, then keep what it used under the descriptor's archive keys -- so what is missing is the key function beside `metal_key::render` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/binary_archive/metal_key.rs:185) for an object-plus-mesh-plus-fragment triple, and the `check` arm that refuses a mesh creation on a miss (`binary_archive::check` is already called for the mesh path at crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/pipeline/render.rs:1579, where the comment says outright that no archive holds a mesh render pipeline). It is deliberately NOT done here: adding `BinaryArchive::add_mesh_render_pipeline_functions` adds an item to a published crate's public surface and a new archive key form to its container, which needs docs/REFUSALS.md regenerated and the `api_surface` table updated, and this stream took no evidence for either. Every venue's: the gap is in the runtime's own API, before any Vulkan call. Open: for whoever takes the runtime's archive surface.

Metal accepts a **metallib** as a binary archive and we refuse it. Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this case's own committed recording over three runs: `newBinaryArchiveWithDescriptor:error:` with the descriptor's `url` set to a metallib of the case's own shader answers an archive, where the same call over a text file, an empty file, a missing path and a directory each answers `MTLBinaryArchiveDomain` code 1 (the four rows this case compares beside it, all four of which we match exactly). What Metal does with such an archive is not measured here -- whether it holds anything, or is simply an empty archive that happens to have read a container it recognises -- and that is the first thing the fix needs. Ours refuses at `container::read` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/binary_archive/container.rs:183), which reads the file whole and hands it to `decode`, whose first act is to check the suite-private magic `M2VBARCH` and a version word (container.rs:116, the magic at :37); a metallib starts `MTLB`, so `decode` answers `None` and the creation becomes `BinaryArchive(InvalidFile)` (container.rs:240). By the owner's standing rule that what Metal allows we must allow, the refusal is the bug. The fix is to decide what a non-archive container means and say so: either accept a file that parses as a metallib as an archive that holds no entry (which is what Metal's answer is consistent with, and which `Library::from_metallib` can already tell), or keep refusing and record an accepted difference in docs/API.md section 10. The first changes a published crate's documented refusal surface -- `Device::new_binary_archive`'s own doc comment states that a file that is missing or not an archive is `BinaryArchive(InvalidFile)` 'as Metal answers for a missing, empty, garbage or text file and for a directory', a list measured on an M3 Max and an M4 that is correct as far as it goes and simply never asked about a metallib -- so it is not this stream's call. Every venue's: the refusal is in the container reader, before any Vulkan call. Open: for whoever takes the runtime's archive surface.

Metal's `MTLAttributeStrideStatic` on a `[[stage_in]]` layout of `MTLBufferLayoutStrideDynamic` is not "read at stride 0"; it fetches the element at the bind offset for the FIRST element and hands every element past it ZERO. Measured on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from these cases' own committed recordings: a dynamic layout over a buffer holding `0x10 + e` at element `e`, eight threads stepping by thread position in x at rate 1, bound with the constant, answered `0x110` and then `0x100` seven times (the fixture writes the attribute plus `0x100`), while a bind at stride 0 answered `0x110` eight times -- so the two are different answers and Metal's validation stops neither. The same shape at a bind offset of 8 answered `0x112` and then `0x100` seven times, which says the bind offset still reaches the first element. Ours answers the stride-0 reading: `attribute_stride` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/argument_table.rs:377) maps the constant to `None`, `None` removes the index's entry from `ArgumentTable::attribute_strides`, and every reader of that map takes a missing entry as 0 -- the binder's push constant `PushField::StageInStride` (crates/metal2vulkan/src/lower/stage_io/stage_in.rs:179, whose own module note at line 28 says "as 0 for a buffer bound without one") and the reach check (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/fetch_reach.rs:112). So the fetch walks elements at stride 0 and every thread reads element 0, which is a silently wrong answer rather than a refusal. The runtime already knows the real behaviour for ONE of the four setters: `ComputeCommandEncoder::set_bytes_with_stride` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/compute.rs:607) documents "an M4 read element 0 of the bytes and zeros past it" and refuses that combination `NotImplemented(KernelStageIn)` rather than emulating it -- this oracle shows the buffer forms behave the same way, so the note on the buffer forms (argument_table.rs:377 and compute.rs:509, "one bound without a stride reads at stride 0") is what is wrong, not the inline-bytes one. The fix belongs in the fetch, not in the table: `PushField::StageInStride` needs to be able to say "the constant was bound" apart from "stride 0" -- a sentinel value or a flag beside it -- and the pulled read in crates/metal2vulkan/src/lower/stage_io/stage_in.rs must then select the element at the bind offset where the element index is 0 and a zero of the attribute's form otherwise, which is the same predicate the inline-bytes form would need and would let that refusal be dropped too. It is deliberately NOT done here: this stream's target is the conformance suite, the change is to a published crate's shader lowering and its push-constant ABI (so it moves `SEMANTICS_VERSION` and every stage-in recording), and it needs release-mode evidence this stream has not taken. Scoped to every venue because the gap is in the push constant and the fetch's own arithmetic, before any device behaviour -- measured on this M3 Max alone, so every other venue is expected and unaudited. Open: for whoever takes the runtime's stage-in fetch.

Metal's `half` result of a 16-bit float texel hands back the texel's own NaN code, with its sign, its payload and its signalling bit kept, and ours answers the one positive quiet NaN `0x7e00` for every one of them. Verified on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this case's own committed recording of plain Metal read against our own codes at every one of the differing words of this run: Metal answers the twelve NaN codes of the case's own `V` table other than `0x7e00` -- `0x7c01`, `0x7d55`, `0x7dff`, `0x7e01`, `0x7f00`, `0x7fff`, `0xfc01`, `0xfdff`, `0xfe00`, `0xfe01`, `0xff00` and `0xffff` -- at 43 texels each and 42 for `0xff00`, which is 515, and ours answers `0x7e00` at all 1,545 differing words of the three sites without exception. No finite, zero, denormal or infinite texel differs anywhere, and the count is the same at all three access sites. The cause is that our `half` texel access reads the image as a `vec4` of `f32` and converts it: `lower/texture/half.rs` takes the image instruction's `f32` texel through `narrow::round_texel`, and the device's decode of a 16-bit float texel into `f32` has already canonicalized the NaN, so the sign and the payload are gone before our conversion ever sees them -- which is why all twelve codes, of both signs, collapse onto the one positive quiet NaN, and why the case's `widened` column, where Metal canonicalizes too, is exact. Metal's `texture2d<half>` read never widens, so the texel's bits survive by construction. This is NOT the same gap as `vertex-format-constant-step`'s and `attribute-format-fetches`' half rows and one fix cannot close both: those run the other way round -- Metal canonicalizes the widen and WE carry the payload and the sign -- so a canonicalizing select after the widen, which is their exact form, leaves this row exactly as it stands, because we already answer the canonical NaN here. What the two share is one device fact, that this chip's half-to-float widening canonicalizes a NaN; there it is what Metal shows and we do not reproduce, here it is what destroys the payload inside our own path. The exact form here is to read a half-float texture through its 16-bit integer alias and assemble the `half` from its bits -- the read side of the `StorageImageClass::HalfBits` aliasing the translator already has for half texel writes (`lower/texture/slice.rs`) -- which changes the slot's view and the sampled path's footprint and costs per-access work, so by the owner's fast-default rule it belongs behind a `DevicePolicy` switch with its docs/FAST-PATHS.md row and a golden-hash re-bless, not in the default path. Announced as `device-nan-encoding`, whose own definition in `pipeline/artifact.rs` says validation derives no tolerance from it, so a tolerance here would be the suite overruling the contract under test and the row stays divergent. Measured on Apple M3 Max alone, which is why the row names this venue: a device whose 16-bit float texel decode keeps the NaN's bits would already agree. Open: translator work, on the orchestrator's todo list.

Metal's stored blend result rounds the SOURCE product to the attachment's precision and carries the DESTINATION product into the sum unrounded -- `round(round(Sf*S) + Df*D)`, one fused multiply-add on the destination term -- and ours is the mirror image, `round(Sf*S + round(Df*D))`, the destination product rounded and the source product fused. Verified by measurement rather than from the notice: this case's own committed recording of plain Metal on this M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) and our own codes at every differing word of this run, both read against the case's own source sweep and destination generator, which a host with no Metal rebuilds. column5: Err(Error::Unsupported("unsupported: Unsupported { feature: Format, needs: NotImplemented, location: None, symbol: Some(\"MTLPixelFormatASTC_4x2_sRGB\") }"))
column6: The runtime holds no image of ASTC's 4x2 and 8x4 footprints, so `heapTextureSizeAndAlignWithDescriptor:` -- CPU arithmetic over a descriptor, which Metal answers for every one of them -- is refused `Unsupported(Format, NotImplemented)` out of the translator's format table (crates/metal2vulkan/src/metal/format/mod.rs, the `formats_named_not_held!` and `astc_without_a_vulkan_block!` patterns, whose `repr` is `NotImplemented`). Measured on an Apple M3 Max under macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal, in a throwaway process forked per (format, texture type): Metal answers a size and an alignment for every descriptor of this case, makes a texture of every format in every texture type bar the ones the case's own module records, and takes a host round trip through each. The whole of Metal's answer is in this case's recording, which is what an implementation will be held to. The case STOPS at this first refusal by design: the runtime refuses all 33 formats of the family, so recording a refusal per site and going on would print some 2900 `Refused` rows and need a ledger row for each. So this one row stands for the family, and the open work -- which formats, and what Metal answers for each -- is on the orchestrator's todo list with the measurements. Scoped `*` and not to a venue: the refusal is decided by the format table before any device is consulted, so no device can change it; verified on MoltenVK over this M3 Max (2026-10-24), unverified elsewhere by execution.

column1: # The memoryless rows of the texture-descriptor crossing family: two distinct gaps, the heap
# size query's and the texture-buffer creator's.

column6: Plain Metal answers `heapTextureSizeAndAlignWithDescriptor:` for a MTLStorageModeMemoryless descriptor and the runtime refuses it `Invalid(StorageMode)`, so every memoryless row of this family is a refusal and no memoryless footprint is compared anywhere. Measured on an Apple M3 Max under macOS 27.0.1, plain Metal with no API validation layer, in a throwaway process forked per shape: Metal answers a memoryless descriptor of EVERY usage this family states (0x0, 0x1, 0x2, 0x3, 0x4, 0x5, 0x11, 0x4000, 0x8000) and EVERY texture type including TextureBuffer and a four-sample multisample one, and the texture it makes answers storageMode 3. The number it answers is the UNCOMPRESSED footprint: 16384 bytes for a 64 by 64 RGBA8Unorm against 16512 in each of the other three storage modes, and 22144 against 22528 at seven levels - the same answer `allowGPUOptimizedContents` off gives, so Memoryless is a third switch into the same lossless-compression gate as PixelFormatView usage and that property. Plain Metal answers 128 bytes of alignment from `heapTextureSizeAndAlignWithDescriptor:` for every descriptor of this family, and we answer 1024 on this driver -- the image's own alignment raised to at least `bufferImageGranularity` and never narrowed back to Metal's. `Device::heap_texture_size_and_align` answers the device image's own footprint wherever that runs past Metal's modelled answer: `heap_plan` widens the model with the image's `VkMemoryRequirements` (`size: size_and_align.size.max(metal.size)`, `align: size_and_align.align.max(metal.align)`, crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/texture/heap.rs), so the number a consumer places textures by is the driver's and not Metal's. A consumer that sizes a heap from Metal's answers and lays its textures out at Metal's offsets UNDER-ALLOCATES here and its placements do not fit. We announce `metal2vulkan-degrade-heap-texture-larger-than-metal` (crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/degradation.rs, `HeapTextureLargerThanMetal`, raised by `degrade_past_metal_size` in the same file as the widening), which says outright that the answer is the device's -- but a recording taken on Metal declares nothing about this venue's driver, so the notice justifies no field here, and by the owner's standing rule that we answer what Metal answers the number is the bug. The exact form already exists for one route, and that is the shape of the fix: where a texture is held as a shadow of Metal's tiles in memory of its own (`AliasRoute::Tiled`, `texture/heap_tiled.rs`'s `shadow_tiles` and `tiles_serve`) the call answers Metal's size and alignment exactly, and Metal's own model is already on the public API as `Device::metal_heap_texture_size_and_align`. What is open is to take that route (or that model) for the descriptors this driver's images decline it on, and to decide which of the two calls crates/metal2vulkan-conformance/src/runtime_side.rs asks for this family and the heap-size families beside it. The refusal is CPU arithmetic over a descriptor before any device call, and this row records it on this venue, which is where this run measured it. This is a distinct gap from the memoryless size-query row beside it: the CREATOR refuses, and deeper -- a texture buffer is made over a buffer, and the `StorageMode::Memoryless => Err(invalid(call, Problem::StorageMode))` arm in crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/buffer.rs has no memoryless backing to give it, where Vulkan's nearest form is the lazily allocated allocation the texture path already uses for a memoryless attachment (`texture/attachment_stand_in.rs`). So the fix is not the size query's: it is a memoryless backing for the buffer a texture buffer lies over, or a texture-buffer creator that does not go through `new_buffer` for this mode. What a memoryless texture buffer's texels do is itself unmeasured -- the host cannot read them and no pass targets a texture buffer -- and measuring it is part of the work. The refusal is in the runtime's own creator before any device call, and this row records it on this venue, which is where this run measured it. Open: runtime work on the orchestrator's todo list.

column6: Plain Metal answers `heapTextureSizeAndAlignWithDescriptor:` for an MTLPixelFormatASTC_4x4_LDR descriptor and we refuse it `NotImplemented(DecodedHeapTexture)`, so this venue compares no heap footprint for any ASTC format. Not a device gap and not an honest lack of a feature: where the device has no ASTC format the runtime already carries such a texture on its own, decoding its blocks into a twin and announcing `metal2vulkan-degrade-carried-decoded-twin` (`Degradation::CarriedDecodedTwin`), and the same run makes and reads plain ASTC textures. What it has not got is the heap form: crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/texture/heap.rs returns `Err(Error::NotImplemented(RuntimeGap::DecodedHeapTexture))` as soon as `crate::astc::decode_of(&plan)` is `Some`, before any layout is computed, and crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/texture.rs refuses the making at the same gap. The reason the type names is that an ASTC carrier's blocks would lie in the heap's own bytes, which the decoded twin would have to decode as the texture is placed, and nothing decides when that decode happens or what a later write to the heap's bytes means for the twin. The fix belongs in those two files together with crates/metal2vulkan-runtime/src/astc.rs: give a decoded twin a placement over heap bytes with a stated decode point, or -- where the device has the format -- stop routing the descriptor through `decode_of` at all. The size query is the cheaper half and is refused only because it shares the arm: it needs no twin, just Metal's modelled footprint for the compressed layout. The refusal is before any device call, and this row records it on this venue, which is where this run measured it. Open: runtime work on the orchestrator's todo list.

Metal's rule is measured, and the one-sample row is what pins `floor` against round-to-nearest: this case's own committed recording, taken on an Apple M3 Max under macOS 27.0.1, holds the destination at every channel (the first differing element is Metal 255 against our 64, the fragment's own 0.25 channel as a code), and the four elements of the site are the one texel's four channels with a bound of 191. The exact form is ours to compute: derive the coverage from the output alpha in the fragment function by Metal's floor rule and write it as the sample mask, ANDed with a mask the fragment already writes (which this family measured Metal to AND, and which a device-computed coverage cannot honour in that order), rather than enabling the device's field. Metal's stored sRGB code and ours differ at this site, and the row's count and bound are this run's. The cause is established and is not half precision: Metal's compiler folds the attachment's blend and its format conversion into the fragment function under fast math, rounding the SOURCE product to the attachment's precision and carrying the DESTINATION product into the sum unrounded -- `round(round(Sf*S) + Df*D)` -- where we leave the blend to the device's fixed-function unit and so compute the mirror image, and the pipeline records `PrecisionNote::HalfOutputFastMathBlend` for it (crates/metal2vulkan/src/pipeline/color_writes.rs, `StageIo::half_fast_colors` in pipeline/stage_io.rs). That rule was measured word by word on an Apple M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this family's own committed recordings, and the file's Apple M3 Max rows carry the measurement. The fix is to fold the blend into the fragment function as Metal's compiler does, computing the attachment's own precision inside the shader; that needs the destination value in the module and moves every such pipeline, so it is translator and pipeline work. `half-output-fast-math-blend`'s own definition in pipeline/artifact.rs says validation derives no tolerance from it, so a tolerance here would be the suite overruling the contract under test and the row stays divergent. This case is the one that blends into an sRGB attachment, through the same owned fast-math fixture (`rt6_samples`), so two conversions sit after the arithmetic rather than one: the blend's own rounding and the linear-to-sRGB encode of the result. The bound is larger than the plain unorm family's for that reason -- a code of linear difference becomes several codes after the encode where the curve is steep -- and this run does NOT separate the two contributions: whether any part of the difference is this device's sRGB encode rather than the unfolded blend is unestablished, and separating them (the same draw into a linear `RGBA8Unorm` target, which `argb8-targets-*` already records on this venue) is the first step of the fix. That rule was measured word by word on an Apple M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this family's own committed recordings, and the file's Apple M3 Max rows carry the measurement. The fix is to fold the blend into the fragment function as Metal's compiler does, computing the attachment's own precision inside the shader; that needs the destination value in the module and moves every such pipeline, so it is translator and pipeline work. `half-output-fast-math-blend`'s own definition in pipeline/artifact.rs says validation derives no tolerance from it, so a tolerance here would be the suite overruling the contract under test and the row stays divergent. Folding no blend is ours on every device, but the codes a given device's blend unit produces are its own, which is why the row names this venue and why its numbers are not the Apple rows'. On this venue the bound at `zero-1msa` and `sas-1msa` is exactly the sign bit (32768 at 16-bit words, 2147483648 at 32-bit ones), which is a zero of the other sign rather than a code of difference; which side holds which sign is NOT established by this run, because the report's bound names the magnitude and not its direction. The cause is established and is not half precision: Metal's compiler folds the attachment's blend and its format conversion into the fragment function under fast math, rounding the SOURCE product to the attachment's precision and carrying the DESTINATION product into the sum unrounded -- `round(round(Sf*S) + Df*D)` -- where we leave the blend to the device's fixed-function unit and so compute the mirror image, and the pipeline records `PrecisionNote::HalfOutputFastMathBlend` for it (crates/metal2vulkan/src/pipeline/color_writes.rs, `StageIo::half_fast_colors` in pipeline/stage_io.rs). That rule was measured word by word on an Apple M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this family's own committed recordings, and the file's Apple M3 Max rows carry the measurement. The fix is to fold the blend into the fragment function as Metal's compiler does, computing the attachment's own precision inside the shader; that needs the destination value in the module and moves every such pipeline, so it is translator and pipeline work. `half-output-fast-math-blend`'s own definition in pipeline/artifact.rs says validation derives no tolerance from it, so a tolerance here would be the suite overruling the contract under test and the row stays divergent. Folding no blend is ours on every device, but the codes a given device's blend unit produces are its own, which is why the row names this venue and why its numbers are not the Apple rows'. The cause is established and is not half precision: Metal's compiler folds the attachment's blend and its format conversion into the fragment function under fast math, rounding the SOURCE product to the attachment's precision and carrying the DESTINATION product into the sum unrounded -- `round(round(Sf*S) + Df*D)` -- where we leave the blend to the device's fixed-function unit and so compute the mirror image, and the pipeline records `PrecisionNote::HalfOutputFastMathBlend` for it (crates/metal2vulkan/src/pipeline/color_writes.rs, `StageIo::half_fast_colors` in pipeline/stage_io.rs). That rule was measured word by word on an Apple M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this family's own committed recordings, and the file's Apple M3 Max rows carry the measurement. The fix is to fold the blend into the fragment function as Metal's compiler does, computing the attachment's own precision inside the shader; that needs the destination value in the module and moves every such pipeline, so it is translator and pipeline work. `half-output-fast-math-blend`'s own definition in pipeline/artifact.rs says validation derives no tolerance from it, so a tolerance here would be the suite overruling the contract under test and the row stays divergent. Folding no blend is ours on every device, but the codes a given device's blend unit produces are its own, which is why the row names this venue and why its numbers are not the Apple rows'. The cause is established and is not half precision: Metal's compiler folds the attachment's blend and its format conversion into the fragment function under fast math, rounding the SOURCE product to the attachment's precision and carrying the DESTINATION product into the sum unrounded -- `round(round(Sf*S) + Df*D)` -- where we leave the blend to the device's fixed-function unit and so compute the mirror image, and the pipeline records `PrecisionNote::HalfOutputFastMathBlend` for it (crates/metal2vulkan/src/pipeline/color_writes.rs, `StageIo::half_fast_colors` in pipeline/stage_io.rs). That rule was measured word by word on an Apple M3 Max (macOS 27.0.1) from this family's own committed recordings, and the file's Apple M3 Max rows carry the measurement. The fix is to fold the blend into the fragment function as Metal's compiler does, computing the attachment's own precision inside the shader; that needs the destination value in the module and moves every such pipeline, so it is translator and pipeline work. `half-output-fast-math-blend`'s own definition in pipeline/artifact.rs says validation derives no tolerance from it, so a tolerance here would be the suite overruling the contract under test and the row stays divergent. Folding no blend is ours on every device, but the codes a given device's blend unit produces are its own, which is why the row names this venue and why its numbers are not the Apple rows'.
